Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: Physical ID is used for KYC at financial institutions (physical presence required). No e-KYC guidelines exist as of 2023 UNCDF diagnostic. Smart Wallet/Mobile ID planned to enable digital KYC for bank account opening but not yet implemented.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: NNI is attributed from birth and linked to civil registry inscriptions (Law No.39/AN/19). Birth registration stands at ~92.6% (2012 survey). RNPP designed to integrate civil registry data. Some amendments to civil registration law still needed per UNFPA assessment.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The national ID card is legally required for obtaining a passport, applying for civil service positions, voter registration, receiving government services and private sector services. ID also required for a newborn birth certificate.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: Law No.39/AN/19 (2019) established the RNPP as a centralised computerised biometric national persons register. Digital ID card database operational since 2014. HSB-implemented social registry ABIS (central fingerprint matching) also in place.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: RNPP was designed with interoperability intent (NNI mandatory for all institutions); however, a 2023 UNCDF diagnostic found identification databases 'fragmented and neither interoperable nor harmonized'. Mobile ID (2026) targets interoperability as a goal.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: Physical national ID required to open a bank account (physical presence mandatory). Only 25-26% of population holds a bank account. Smart Wallet (Visa/TECH5 MoU, 2025) aims to enable digital financial inclusion via Mobile ID but not yet implemented.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: First issuance of digital ID card costs 2,700 DJF (~$15 USD); renewal costs 2,000 DJF (~$11 USD). A fee is charged for both first issuance and renewal; not free.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: NNI assigned from birth (RNPP Law 2019). National ID card issued from age 18. Children registered in civil registry receive NNI. No evidence of a child-specific ID credential below 18.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Holding a national ID card is mandatory for all Djiboutian citizens (presidential decree 2009; all citizens required to hold digital card by end-2015). NNI use is compulsory for all institutions. Voter registration, passport, and government services require the ID.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: RNPP Law (2019) explicitly includes 'any foreigner residing regularly on national territory'. Police department issues residence/identity cards to foreigners. Refugees covered under 2017 National Refugee Law for basic services access.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: Social registry linked to ID system (World Bank/HSB project; up to 1M enrolled); SEAS uses social registry in 9 government programs. ID required for government benefits. World Bank social safety net programs use the registry for targeting.
